description: A Source is a fragment IRI on its item, exactly like a Review: <item-IRI>#source-<n> in authored order (AGSC-05-14), which keeps the dataset blank-node-free without any URL-to-IRI escaping question and works for a urn:agsc:channel: resource too. The citation is composed from named keys — dcterms:source from resource, dcterms:title/creator/date from title/author/year — never from an unspecified bibliographicCitation string; asc:verifiedOn renders the date as that day's midnight instant, and asc:grade carries the grade. `nquads` is the complete canonical N-Quads serialization of the vector's input (tests/vectors/README.md, Expected shapes), so it also carries the item's own rdf:type/skos:inScheme/skos:prefLabel and the reachability edge `asc:source` that connects the item to its Source (AGSC-05-14, AGSC-05-27) — without it the Source node would be an orphan no consumer could associate with its item. N-Quads lines are sorted by their serialized bytes. Plain literals carry ^^xsd:string in N-Quads (AGSC-05-31 form c). The graph term: every line is a quad whose fourth term is the Bundle IRI `<https://example.org/>` (AGSC-04-15), written as ` <https://example.org/>` before the terminating ` .` of each line; because every line carries the same graph term, the lines are in the byte order of their triples. Expected values are derived by hand from the rule text.
